Baranwal et al., arXiv:2209.09223v1, Theorem 11, Proposition 18 and proof of Theorem 19
Independent exact determinant, bounded cyclic enumeration and symbolic run count
correctness.rationale: Baranwal et al. Proposition 18 excludes 001011 from periodic good points (an occurrence forces the nonperiodic exceptional configuration); complementation excludes 110100. The proof of their Theorem 19 supplies the exact remaining finite forbidden set F and its equivalent difference windows G. The local equivalence works for periodic windows even at lengths shorter than the forbidden words. Each allowed cyclic difference code is all zero or has one-runs of length two or four separated by at least two zeros; the all-one code is forbidden. Its parity is even, so integration by XOR gives exactly two complementary origin-marked periodic lifts. The independently reconstructed ten-state code graph has det(I-zA)=1-z-z^4-z^6 by exact signed-subset determinant and agrees with exhaustive cyclic counts through n=12. Alternatively, independently count codes with k>0 one-runs by marking a run start. Each length-n code can be marked in k ways, and there are n coordinate choices for the mark followed by k blocks of generating function W=(z^4+z^6)/(1-z). Thus nonconstant codes contribute sum_{k>=1} W^k/k to sum C_n z^n/n, and all-zero codes contribute -log(1-z). This gives -log(1-z-z^4-z^6), and the two lifts square the zeta denominator. Formal logarithmic differentiation and inversion of P_n=sum_{d|n}d O_d give the stated enumerators. The first 16 counts agree. Only zero difference codes occur at lengths 1–3, and 11 followed by n-2 zeros has least period n for n>=4 (one cyclic one-run start); a lift's period would also be a period of its differences. This proves the claimed least periods for all n. Replay: the frozen verify.py and certificate.json specify the finite graph/count checks; the independent computation constructed the length-four graph directly from G and used a signed-subset determinant rather than Newton identities. The separate F-matrix certificate was inspected, not required for the all-n proof above.
residual_risks: Bounded direct antisquare tests are not substitutes for the all-orders language reduction. The zeta does not claim the entire good shift is of finite type or count its nonperiodic points.
Strict attribution: Theorem 19 formally states finite-word growth; its proof supplies the forbidden languages and finite-word recurrence.

Independent periodic count and primitive-period argument
value.rationale: Marked periodic points and primitive periods are natural invariants of this two-sided avoidance shift. The exact rational zeta and least-period support answer questions the finite-word growth rate alone cannot answer: which orbit lengths occur and how many marked or primitive orbits there are at every length. The cyclic lifting multiplicity and the separation of exceptional nonperiodic words make the calculation specific to this shift, rather than a restatement of its published growth polynomial.
residual_risks: This is a periodic classification only, not a description of the nonperiodic dynamics.
